The claim that the Indian government is providing free laptops to all students under the 'PM Free Laptop Scheme 2026' is false. The Press Information Bureau (PIB) Fact Check has repeatedly debunked such claims, stating that the Government of India has not announced any such scheme. [1] [2] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7] These viral messages, often circulated on social media and WhatsApp, are scams designed to collect personal information. [1] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7] [8] [9] [10]

While there is no central government scheme providing free laptops to all students, some Indian states do have their own laptop or tablet distribution programs for eligible students. [1] Examples include Tamil Nadu's "Ulagam Ungal Kaiyil" scheme and Uttar Pradesh's "Swami Vivekananda Yuva Sashaktikaran Yojana (Mission DigiShakti)". [1] These state-level schemes have specific eligibility criteria and are managed through state education departments. [1]

Regarding the claim that one must click on the link www.pm-free-laptop-yojana.in to register for the 'PM Free Laptop Scheme 2026', this is also false and part of the scam. [1] [11] [3] [12] [4] [5] [6] [7] [8] Official government websites in India typically end with ".gov.in". [11] [8] [13] Fraudulent websites often use attractive offers like free laptops to lure individuals into sharing personal details, which can then be used for phishing or other scams. [11] [4] [6] [14] [8] [9] The PIB Fact Check unit advises citizens to verify information through official government sources and not to click on suspicious links or share personal information on unverified platforms.
